page: Microsoft Azure E4_v4 is an Ev4-family virtual machine configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz, the underlying hardware features 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, providing 2 threads per core. The CPU cache architecture includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache. This instance operates on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and utilizes the x86_64 architecture. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate that the E4_v4 sits primarily in the lower performance tiers for compute-heavy tasks. The stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU tests place the instance in the bottom 25% of benchmarked servers, with scores of 1409.99 and 3698.58 respectively. Memory bandwidth tests show a significant performance drop-off when transitioning from cached to uncached operations; small-block cached read bandwidth is 206.51 GB/sec (bottom 25%), whereas large-block uncached read bandwidth drops to 23.02 GB/sec, placing it in the bottom 10%. Similarly, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark database operations register in the bottom 10% and bottom 25% respectively, highlighting a performance bottleneck under heavy concurrent processing or database workloads.

With 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, the E4_v4 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio, making it a memory-optimized instance class. While its raw compute and memory bandwidth benchmarks are relatively weak, the high memory density provides qualitative cost efficiency for workloads that require large memory footprints but have modest CPU demands. This makes the instance suitable for relational databases with small active datasets, caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that do not require high-throughput parallel processing.
description: Microsoft Azure E4_v4 is an Ev4-family memory-optimized virtual machine featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, running on an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor at 2.6 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture with Microsoft Hyper-V, it provides 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core, but lacks local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks place this instance mostly in the bottom 25% for compute and memory bandwidth, with uncached large-block read bandwidth dropping to the bottom 10% at 23.02 GB/sec. Despite these compute limitations, its high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core offers qualitative resource density for memory-bound tasks. The E4_v4 is suited for memory-intensive workloads with moderate CPU requirements, such as caching layers, small relational databases, and enterprise applications.
